answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by pricing identity in slashable stake: each new agent posts a ferrous collateral bond locking real value behind its pseudonym, while registration is throttled like marble gates admitting newcomers only in measured batches. Reputation accrues through countersigned work, so a cloned identity starts weightless as a gale-blown leaf and must pay for every shard of trust. When two agents collude to double-sign, both bonds are slashed and the bounty flows to detectors, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
